1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of light pulses having a first speed via __modulated infrared radiation__; receiving a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle __via an infrared video sensor__; and transmitting a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, __wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed__.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle __such that the second speed is__ slower than the first speed.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed __and wherein the third speed is determined based on absence of receipt of light pulse sequences from the vehicle__.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth speed is different from the second speed __and is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the vehicle and the third vehicle__.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Original) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Original) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses.

11. (Currently Amended) An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a __non-transitory__ memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of light pulses having a first speed __via modulated infrared radiation__; receive a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle __via an infrared video sensor__; and transmit a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, __wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed__.

12. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle __such that the second speed is__ slower than the first speed.

13. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed __and wherein the third speed is determined based on absence of receipt of light pulse sequences from the vehicle__.

14. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 13, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth speed is different from the second speed __and is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the vehicle and the third vehicle__.

15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulse are received from one or more vehicles.

20. (Original) The apparatus of claim 19, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses.
